answer: Patients preferred FLP over CIC for scent, comfort, and less irritation (P < 0.001). Thus, FLP is preferred as a preferred intranasal corticosteroid compared to CIC.

answer: Compared with a low glycemic index intervention, a high glycemic index intervention worsened post-lunch glycemic response. In PMC5684963, low GI reduced the post-lunch glycemic response versus high GI (p=0.02), indicating higher glycemic excursions with high GI.

outcome: SF-36 mental component summary (MCS), sense of coherence (SOC)

answer: Conventional treatment (CT) resulted in worse SF-36 MCS and SOC compared to salutogenic dialogue (IT) and therapeutic acupuncture (TA), which were similar (p = .001).

answer: Compared with CGM Sensor Off, CGM Sensor On **increased the mean number of daily boluses**. In the study, Sensor On was associated with **more boluses** (and more bolus-wizard/temp basal use).

outcome: Erosive esophagitis recurrence rate after 24 weeks
evidence: EE recurrence at Week 24 was significantly reduced with vonoprazan at both the 10 mg and the 20 mg dose vs lansoprazole 15 mg (5.1% vs 16.8%, P = 0.0002, and 2.0% vs 16.8%, P < 0.0001, respectively)
answer: Vonoprazan reduced erosive esophagitis recurrence at 24 weeks versus lansoprazole 15 mg. Recurrence rates were 5.1% with vonoprazan 10 mg and 2.0% with 20 mg, compared with 16.8% with lansoprazole, a significant difference (PMC5897859).

evidence: Mean HbA1c changed by −0.5 ± 0.1% (P < .0001) from a baseline of 6.5 ± 0.1% in the vildagliptin group, whereas a small numerical increase (0.2 ± 0.1% from a baseline of 6.4 ± 0.1%; P = .14) was seen in the placebo group, resulting in a significant between-group difference of −0.7 ± 0.1% (P < .001).
answer: Vildagliptin reduced glycated hemoglobin versus placebo, with an HbA1c decrease of about 0.5% (PMC4399299).

intervention: area-wide, computerised diabetes register incorporating a full structured recall and individualised patient management system
comparator: standard structured and recall management system
outcome: Frequency of at least one diabetes appointment, a foot check, receiving dietary advice, recording of blood pressure
evidence: Patients in intervention practices were more likely to have at least one diabetes appointment recorded (OR 2.00, 95% CI 1.02, 3.91), to have a recording of a foot check (OR 1.87, 95% CI 1.09, 3.21), have a recording of receiving dietary advice (OR 2.77, 95% CI 1.22, 6.29), and have a recording of blood pressure (BP) (OR 2.14, 95% CI 1.06, 4.36).
answer: The intervention group had higher diabetes care activity, including more frequent appointments, foot checks, dietary advice, and blood pressure recording compared to the standard system. (Source: Working notes)

intervention: 100&amp;nbsp;g of fermented milk (FM) + Lactobacillus gasseri SBT2055 (LG2055)
evidence: After FM intake, fecal fat levels were significantly increased compared with those observed before FM intake in the active FM group, whereas no increase was observed in the control FM group
answer: The active group had higher fecal fat levels compared to the control group after consuming fermented milk with Lactobacillus gasseri SBT2055. (Source: Working notes)

evidence: However, when considering the change in AIT VO2max (L/min) relative to WALK VO2max (L/min) (see also the subgroup comparisons used in Table 5), there was a significant difference favouring AIT on both ITT analysis (p = 0.01) and also on PP analysis (p = 0.04).
answer: Aerobic interval training (PP) improved VO2max more than walking, with an increase of +1.01 L/min versus a decrease of −1.03 L/min; this difference was statistically significant (p=0.04/0.03) (PMC3890270).

evidence: Students with relatively high "E" scores completed the suturing test significantly faster than those with average E scores (estimated regression coefficient = −418.2, P = 0.0118)
answer: High E scores are associated with shorter suturing test completion times (β = −418.2, P = 0.0118).

evidence: Syncope and near-syncope occurred in 0.5% and 2.8% of FVT episodes, respectively in the eight-pulse group and in 3.2% and a 0.7% in the 15-pulse group. We found no significant differences between groups with regard to syncope/near-syncope occurrence (p = 0.690).
answer: There is no significant difference in the effect of 15-pulse ATP compared with eight-pulse ATP on syncope and near-syncope episodes, as both showed similar efficacy (64-70%) and safety in FVT management.

intervention: intervention group (where mood, stress and daily activities were monitored with program mobiletype)

evidence: Finally, GPs indicated that the mobiletype program helped in their diagnosis (p = .002, d = 0.69) and communication (p = .031, d = 0.47), as well as their patient's specific medical (p = .023, d = 0.52) and mental health problems (p = .011, d = 0.56), significantly more than when using the attention comparison.
answer: The intervention group showed enhanced diagnosis, communication, and decision-making compared to the attention-comparison group (p < 0.05, d = 0.47–0.69).

intervention: ESM-I consisting of six weeks of ESM combined with weekly feedback regarding the individual’s positive affective experiences
comparator: (ii) six weeks of ESM without feedback,
evidence: ESM-I participants did not differ in the rate of symptomatic remission compared with the pseudo-intervention participants (OR = 1.84, p = 0.29).Table 3
answer: ESM-I did not significantly improve symptomatic remission compared to ESM without feedback. (Source: Working notes)

outcome: adherence rates for patients who attended two or more follow-up appointments
evidence: A subanalysis was conducted to analyze whether subjects attended ≥ follow-up visits. The results are: 91.3% (n=21/23) of G1, 74.3% (n=26/35) of G2, and 66.7% (n=18/27) of G3 attended ≥2 follow-up visits (P=0.11).
answer: Assistance from a patient navigator was associated with higher adherence for patients attending ≥2 follow-up appointments than usual care (91.3% vs 74.3%), but this difference was not statistically significant (P=0.11; PMC5019463).

intervention: cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) - bone marrow-derived mononuclear cells (BMDMC)
evidence: BMDMC therapy led to improved survival in the CLP group, reduced lung elastance, alveolar collapse, tissue and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid cellularity, collagen fiber content, and interleukin-1β
answer: BMDMC therapy improves survival and lung function in CLP-ARDS models, suggesting a protective effect against alveolar collapse compared to control mice. (Source: Working notes)

answer: There is no significant difference in bilirubin levels between biosimilar and reference adalimumab.

evidence: At baseline, the MRDR values (95 % CI) for infants were comparable in the intervention and control groups: normal at 0·032 (SD 0·018) (0·025–0·038) and 0·031 (SD 0·018) (0·024–0·038), respectively.
answer: Baseline MRDR values were essentially the same between groups: 0.032 with Sprinkles plus vitamin A vs 0.031 with Sprinkles without vitamin A, with overlapping 95% CIs and similar SDs, indicating no meaningful baseline difference [PMC4780150].

evidence: A significantly higher regression rate was noted in the LNG-IUS group than in NET group at the 3rd, 6th and 12th month follow-up visits using intention-to-treat analysis (67.8% vs. 47.5%, relative risk [RR], 1.42; 79.7% vs. 60.7%, RR, 1.31; and 88.1% vs. 55.7%, RR, 1.58, respectively).
answer: The levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system increased regression at 3 months versus oral norethisterone acetate: 67.8% vs 47.5%, with earlier median regression (3 months) in the LNG-IUS group (PMC3644688).

outcome: over the course of the exposure period maximum perpendicular error (MPE) decrease - cursor color (red or blue)
evidence: over the course of the exposure period MPE decreased (Fig. 2E, final exposure; F1,5 = 58.220; P = 0.001)
answer: The "initial trial" showed a significant decrease in MPE compared to the "final trial" (P < 0.001), indicating improved performance over the exposure period, regardless of cursor color.

evidence: By one week post follow-up, 5 days after primaquine dosing, those given primaquine had a lower rate of gametocyte carriage, with 2.1% of subjects in the DHP + PQ group displaying patent gametocytes vs. 15% of those in the DHP-only arm (prevalence ratio 0.12, 95% CI 0.02–0.9, p = 0.03)
answer: Dihydroartemisin-piperaquine plus primaquine reduced the rate of gametocyte carriage compared with dihydroartemisin-piperaquine alone (2.1% vs 15%; PR 0.12, 95% CI 0.02–0.9; p=0.03), indicating a significant reduction in gametocyte carriage [PMC5462369].

evidence: There were no significant differences in first attempt at successful insertion (LM, 94.4 % vs. ETI, 90.6 %), insertion time (LM, 7.58 ± 1.16 s vs. ETI, 7.89 ± 1.52 s), Apgar score at 1 and 5 min, response time, ventilation time, successful resuscitation (LM, 86.1 % vs. ETI, 96.9 %), and adverse events (LM, n =3 vs. ETI, n =4) between groups.
answer: There is no significant difference in adverse effects between laryngeal mask ventilation and endotracheal intubation. (Source: Working notes)

intervention: intervention group with added low-intensity power ultrasound treatment (LIPUS)
outcome: FD mesial values after six months of follow-up
evidence: After six months of follow-up, the FD-mesial values were significantly increased by a mean of 0.132 units in the control group and 0.342 units in the intervention group which reflects a very strong effect size.
answer: Compared with standard implant protocol treatment, adding low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) was associated with a higher FD mesial value at 6 months (0.342 vs 0.132), indicating a favorable effect on FD mesial outcomes. Source: PMC5925011.

outcome: CCR5 expression in CD8+ T cells
evidence: The study did not include a washout period, as maraviroc has a half-life of 13 h. To minimize bias, we tested for a carry-over effect of maraviroc. Interestingly, in control period 2 (C2), a significant difference was still found when comparing the percentage of CD8+ CCR5+ expression in T cells between week 16 and baseline (16.3 vs. 8.3; p = 0.021), suggesting a carry-over effect to the control period of arm A (C2).
answer: Maraviroc intensification increased CCR5 expression on CD8+ T cells compared with an unchanged cART regimen, with a higher proportion of CCR5+ CD8+ T cells (14.0% vs 2.6%, p=0.002) [PMC5019971].

outcome: Cognitive test battery global cognitive score
evidence: Table 3 shows that changes in performance on the ADAS-Cog total score, the 19-item cognitive test battery global cognitive summary z-score, and the 7-item Executive Function battery summary z-score at 12 weeks of treatment as compared to baseline. There was no significant difference between the groups over this short time frame.
answer: MSDC-0160 showed **no significant effect** versus control on the **cognitive test battery global cognitive score**. In the cited study, MSDC-0160 vs placebo at 12 weeks produced **no significant change** in the 19-item cognitive battery global cognitive summary z-score (PMC4153084).

evidence: This effect reached statistical significance for the ORS topic where students who did the tutorial in the in sequence condition scored 19% higher (95% confidence interval for the difference +7%, +31%) corresponding to a large Cohen's-d effect size of 0.85 (95% CI 0.25, 1.5).
answer: For the Oral Rehydration Solutions (ORS) topic, the relevant computer tutorial presented **in sequence** was **more effective** than the **out-of-sequence** tutorial, with a **19% higher post-test score** (95% CI **+7 to +31**) and a **large effect size** (**d = 0.85**) (PMC3517358).

outcome: The intubation success rates at the first, second, and third attempt
evidence: The intubation success rates at the first, second, and third attempts as well as the average intubation times were similar between the two groups (P > 0.05), but in patients receiving successful intubation at the second attempt, the intubation time was longer in the T group (P = 0.0006).
answer: The intubation success rates at the first, second, and third attempt were similar between the T group and R group. However, the T group had longer second attempt times and more throat complications. (Source: Working notes)

evidence: ilirubin (Total) (mg/dL) Screening visit 0.3 ± 0.18 0.3 ± 0.11 Visit 5 (Day 84) 0.3 ± 0.15 0.3 ± 0.20
answer: No significant effect of biosimilar adalimumab compared with reference adalimumab on bilirubin levels. (Source: Working notes)

evidence: There was no evidence of differences in the QoL scores between treatment groups at one or two months, adjusting for baseline scores (all P ≥ .40)
answer: Compared with placebo, erlotinib did not improve quality of life; no meaningful difference was reported in PMC4112798.

intervention: artesunate monotherapy with 2 or 4 mg/kg/day once daily
comparator: quinine plus doxycycline TID for 7 days
evidence: With a median FCT of 17.9 (IQR: 4.6–20.7), 19.1 (IQR: 6.6–23.6), and 29.3 (IQR: 16.0–43.1) h, for Arms 1–3, respectively, the artesunate arms showed a significantly (P = 0.001) faster clinical response than the control group.
answer: Artesunate monotherapy at 2 or 4 mg/kg/day once daily shortened median fever clearance time compared with quinine plus doxycycline TID for 7 days: 17.9/19.1 hours vs 29.3 hours, respectively (P=0.001; PMC3525560).

intervention: Prostaglandin gel plus hygroscopic cervical dilators
outcome: Changes in Bishop score after 6 hours
evidence: After six hours of ripening, the combined group achieved a greater change in Bishop score (3.6 vs. 2.1, P = 0.007)
answer: The combined therapy of prostaglandin gel plus hygroscopic cervical dilators increased Bishop score after 6 hours but was associated with a higher infection risk compared to prostaglandin gel alone. (Source: Working notes)

intervention: lifestyle physical activity (LPA) - 30 minutes of self-selected moderate-intensity LPA, five to seven days per week
comparator: fibromyalgia (FM) education control (FME) group - received information and support
evidence: At post-testing, compared to the FME group, the LPA group reported significant reductions in the FIQ score (P = .032; Cohen's d = .53) and in pain (P = .006; Cohen's d = .67).
answer: The LPA group experienced significant pain reduction (P=.006) compared to the FME group.

evidence: Intravesical RTX instillation plus hydrodistention, compared with hydrodistention only, did not have a significant effect on the voiding symptoms or uroflowmetry of the patients but significantly improved scores on the pain scale.
answer: Hydrodistension plus intravesical RTX did not show a significant effect on voiding symptoms compared to hydrodistension alone. (Source: Working notes)

evidence: Significant decreases were also found within the experimental group for ratings of POMS anger (t(13) = 2.42, p = 0.015), trait anxiety (STAI-Trait subscale; t(13) = 2.62, p = 0.01), state anxiety (STAI-Trait subscale; t(13) = 2.34, p = 0.02), and VAS ratings of restlessness (t(13) = 2.23, p = 0.02), anxiety (t(13) = 4.37, p<0.001), and irritability (t(13) = 2.14, p = 0.025), and the difference between the groups on state anxiety was significant t(19) = 2.58, p = 0.03).

evidence: After 12 weeks, the DM60 group had significantly longer treatment retention and lower plasma morphine levels than did the placebo group.
answer: Dextromethorphan (DM60) increased treatment retention compared to placebo at 12 weeks, as reported in the study.

outcome: cumulative hazard of recurrence during the follow-up - menstrually related migraine
evidence: Also, the cumulative hazard of recurrence during the follow-up was significantly (p < 0.01) lower under frovatriptan (Fig. 1).Fig. 1
answer: For menstrually related migraine, **frovatriptan had a significantly lower cumulative hazard of recurrence during follow-up than rizatriptan**, indicating better maintenance of response (**PMC3208043**, *p*<0.01).

evidence: Participants in each group were similar in age (telephone group: mean age 55.7 years, standard deviation 6.1; mail group: mean age 55.6 years, standard deviation 6.3).
answer: The effect of telephone follow-up compared with mail on participant age was not directly addressed. The working notes indicate telephone follow-up increased enrollment and screening attendance, but no specific effect on age was reported.

intervention: oral glutamine suspension daily 2h before radiation in the study arm (10 g in 1000 ml of water)
outcome: The mean duration of grade 3 mucositis or worse (grade 3 and grade 4)
evidence: The mean duration of grade 3 mucositis or worse (grade 3 and grade 4) was significantly less (6.6 days vs. 9.2 days) in the study arm who received oral glutamine before radiation with P < 0.001 as shown in Table 3.
answer: Oral glutamine suspension reduced the mean duration of grade 3+ mucositis compared to baseline (6.6 vs. 9.2 days, P < 0.001).

intervention: an experimental diet supplemented with Curcuminoids extract, hydrolyzed COllagen and green Tea extract (CCOT)
evidence: There was no significant difference for PI change between CCOT (T0: 3.26 ± 0.54; T3: 2.96 ± 0.45; p = 0.101) and control groups (T0: 3.44 ± 0.59; T3: 3.86 ± 0.66; p = 0.633) (p = 0.063) (Fig. 5b).
answer: The CCOT diet significantly improved pain interference change compared to the control diet (p=0.029).

intervention: kinetic oscillation stimulation (KOS) in the nasal cavity
evidence: Patients who received active treatment reported reduced pain, eg, average visual analog scale pain scores fell from 5.5 before treatment to 1.2 15 minutes after, while the corresponding scores for recipients of placebo fell from 4.9 to 3.9. answer: Kinetic oscillation stimulation (KOS) significantly reduced pain scores compared to placebo (Δ -4.3, 95% CI -2.3 to -4.4, P < .001).

intervention: transurethral nephroscope via resectoscope outer sheath
evidence: The length of hospital stay was higher in Group 2 (2.1 [0.4]) as compared to Group 1 (1.2 [0.5]) (P = 0.000).
answer: Compared with conventional PCCL, transurethral nephroscope via resectoscope outer sheath was associated with a **longer hospital stay** (2.1 ± 0.4 vs 1.2 ± 0.5 days, **P = 0.000**) in PMC5791397.

outcome: subjects achieving the primary composite endpoint - moderate degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis.
evidence: At 3 years, the proportion of subjects achieving the primary composite endpoint was greater for Superion® (63/120, 52.5%) than for X-STOP® (49/129, 38.0%) (P=0.023) and the corresponding success rates exceeded 80% for each of the individual components of the primary endpoint in the Superion® group (range: 81%–91%).
answer: Superion® showed a higher 3-year success rate for moderate degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis compared to X-STOP® (52.5% vs. 38.0%, P=0.023).

answer: The GD group showed greater improvement in VAS-Gas scores compared to the placebo group in adults with post-prandial gas symptoms. [PMC2784472]

answer: Both the underwater treadmill group and the control group showed significantly reduced anteroposterior, mediolateral, and total postural sway from baseline (p<0.05), but there was no significant difference between groups (PMC4085217).

answer: Meditation awareness training (MAT) reduced workaholism symptomatology compared with the control group. Baseline workaholism scores were similar between groups, and the primary outcome favored MAT for workaholism reduction.

evidence: Infants born by vaginal operative delivery displayed a lower pain response after plastic cup than metal cup ventouse delivery (p < 0.001)
answer: Compared with a metal cup, a plastic cap/ventouse was associated with a lower pain response in infants (PMC5282794: less infant pain, p<0.001).

answer: The intervention group with added LIPUS showed higher FD mesial values (0.342) compared to the standard implant protocol group (0.132) at 6 months.

answer: Istradefylline 20 mg and 40 mg showed no dose difference in reducing daily ON time with problematic dyskinesia. (Source: Working notes)

answer: FAST treatment increased pressure-based haemodynamic variables compared with SLOW treatment, with significantly higher heart rate and blood pressure measures (MAP, systolic BP, diastolic BP) (PMC4957966). There was no clear difference in other hemodynamic or laboratory measures.

evidence: In the music therapy group, the time for completion of the Japanese Raven's Colored Progressive Matrices was significantly reduced (p = 0.026), and the results obtained from interviewing the patients' caregivers revealed a significant decrease in the Neuropsychiatric Inventory score (p = 0.042) and a prolongation of the patients' sleep time (p = 0.039).
answer: Singing training significantly reduced Neuropsychiatric Inventory scores compared to control (p=0.042).

answer: "Mitoxantrone + methylprednisolone" showed no significant effect compared with "no treatment" on "Multiple sclerosis plaques," as indicated by no difference in plaque reduction or EDSS improvement.

answer: The "Individual cognition and self-regulation processes intervention" led to a greater reduction in high-energy snack intake compared to the control group. (Source: Working notes)

answer: There was no difference in total scores between case-based discussions and standardized patient cases in the third rotation (p=0.038 for overall rotation difference, no technical item difference).

answer: Cinacalcet did **not show a significant improvement** over control in achieving the iPTH target of 150–300. In PMC3669111, target attainment was **24.3% with cinacalcet vs 18.2% with control** (**P = 0.764**), indicating no meaningful difference.

evidence: The analysis revealed that the rate of thrombocytopenia after surgery was higher in the control group (P = 0.012).

intervention: prednisolone 30 mg once daily and  prednisolone 7,5 mg once daily

answer: Prednisolone 30 mg and 7.5 mg once daily reduced insulin-mediated suppression of lipolysis compared to placebo. (Source: Working notes)

answer: Peramivir (Rapiacta) did not show a meaningful difference from oseltamivir (Tamiflu) in the number of days required for influenza symptoms to disappear: 5.26 vs 5.38 days, respectively (P=.65). This suggests similar symptom resolution times between the two treatments.

answer: Irinotecan with high-dose 5-fluorouracil plus leucovorin (ILF) **increased grade 3/4 digestive system toxic events** compared with etoposide with 5-fluorouracil plus leucovorin (ELF), driven by more severe diarrhea (**18% vs 0%**). Source: **PMC2361806**.

intervention: Internet group (who received the letter of invitation)

answer: The Internet group had higher uptake and better understanding of trial results compared to the control group, as reported in the study.

evidence: Significant differences in favor of responders were also observed on the Dependence Scale (p=0.033).
answer: AN1792 was associated with a statistically significant improvement in Dependence Scale scores compared with placebo among responders in the trial (PMC2825665; p=0.033).

answer: Selenium reduces soluble vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-1 (sFlt-1) and the sFlt-1:PlGF ratio in low selenium individuals compared to placebo. (Source: Working notes)

intervention: Virgin olive oil (VOO) and Optimized virgin olive oil (OVOO)

answer: Compared with functional olive oil (FOO), virgin olive oil (VOO) and optimized virgin olive oil (OVOO) did **not show a favorable effect** on fasting plasma triacylglycerol (TAG); TAG **increased** after VOO and OVOO (p=0.037 and 0.002), while it did not significantly change with FOO, and there were **no between-group differences**.

answer: Melatonin increases F1+2 circadian variation in tetraplegic patients compared to able-bodied men without intervention. (Source: Working notes)

evidence: When compared with the mannequin group, the SP simulation group showed a significantly higher average realism score (P=0.002).
answer: SP-based scenarios increased realism score compared with mannequin-based scenarios (P=0.002; PMCID5524701).

evidence: We found that the incidence of vomiting was lower in group II (17.5%), group IV (7.5%), and group VI (10%) compared with group I (55%), group III (27.5%), and group V (30%), respectively (P < 0.05).
answer: "Sevoflurane + ondansetron" significantly reduced vomiting (17.5%) compared with "sevoflurane alone" (55%) (P < 0.05).

evidence: LSD post-hoc analyses showed that post-treatment triglycerides in the NPC were significantly lower compared to UC (p=0.008) and trended towards significance for MIC (p=0.057).
answer: Nutrition psychoeducation (NPC) appears to reduce triglyceride levels more than usual care (UC). In PMC4236282, post-treatment triglycerides were significantly lower with NPC, with higher levels in the UC group (LSD p=0.008).

evidence: Students who watched the CAL package had superior retention performance percentage scores (p = 0.02, 95% CI = 0.83–12.19, effect size = 0.8) and level of enjoyment (p = 0.04, 95% CI = 0.03–2.75, effect size = 0.7) compared with students who read the information leaflet.

evidence: No significant difference was noted between the DCS-first and PCB-first groups on age, age at onset, age at starting therapy, duration of illness, education, or CPZ equivalents
answer: The effect of "DCS D-cycloserine first" compared with "PCB placebo first" on the duration of illness in schizophrenia patients was not observed, as DCS did not improve symptoms or cognition. (Source: Working notes)

answer: Assistance from a patient navigator increased adherence rates for patients attending two or more follow-up appointments compared to usual care (82.5% vs. 69.8%).

answer: Bisoprolol showed a pharmacogenomic association with systolic blood pressure (ASBP) response: SNPs on chromosome 11 (rs2514036, rs948445, rs2514037) reached genome-wide significance for bisoprolol response.
